newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent firms on cold U.S., OPEC comments.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent firms on cold U.S., OPEC comments.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were firmer on Monday amid continued forecasts for colder weather in the U.S. and a call by the OPEC president to restrain oil output, traders said.
June Brent was trading 25 cents a barrel firmer at 1147 GMT and stood at $18.17, while May gas oil was $1.25 up at $164.50 a tonne.
Independent forecasters Weather Services Corp said temperatures in the U.S. were likely to remain below normal in the next 10 days and traders said this would provide a prop for prices.
OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman said on Monday that OPEC President Abdalla el-Badri had called on OPEC members to restrain oil output to help support sagging world oil prices.
"The president has been calling and asking members to exercise restraint," Lukman said, but added it was not yet clear whether the member countries would respond.
A broker at the IPE said this had had an influence, albeit a small one.
"Lukman's comments are just supporting what has happened," he said.
"We have been range trading between $17.50 and $18.50 and we have been here many times before. It is just a quietish Monday morning."
Traders in the physical markets said business was dull with no cargoes changing hands in early business, but intermonth spreads were firmer.

They said millions of barrels of West African crudes were heading for Asia and this may provide a shot in the arm for North Sea crudes, which are more likely to fill trans-Atlantic requirements in place of West Africa crude oil.
The Iraqi news agency said on Monday that helicopters would be sent to pick up Iraqi Moslem pilgrims from the Saudi border despite a U.S. and allied ban on Iraqi flights in the area.
Brokers played down the influence of this on crude oil prices. "It has not seemed to have had much of an effect," one said.

Technical analysts said they were still bearish in the slightly longer term because of chart gaps on the June contract and the continuation chart. The first of these gaps will weigh in at $18.40 a barrel.
